title: Die Lorelei (first two stanzas)
author: Heinrich Heine
meter: Ballad quatrains, alternating iambic tetrameter / trimeter
source_notes: From 'Buch der Lieder' (1827). English translation by Mark Twain, published in 'A Tramp Abroad', 1880.
reading_notes: Heine reworks the Rhine legend of a siren on the cliff whose singing lures sailors to wreck. The opening 'Ich weiß nicht...' is among the most quoted lines in German literature. Schumann and Silcher both set it to music; Silcher's version became a national folk-song.

lines.original: Ich weiß nicht, was soll es bedeuten,
lines.english: I cannot divine what it meaneth,
lines.gloss: Ich = 'I' (nominative); weiß = 'know' (1st sg. of wissen); nicht = 'not'; was = 'what' (relative); soll = 'shall, should' (modal); es = 'it'; bedeuten = 'to mean' (infinitive).

lines.english: That I should be so sad;
A fable of old time haunts me,
lines.gloss: Ein Märchen = 'a fairy-tale, legend' (nominative neuter); aus = 'from' (+dative); alten Zeiten = 'old times' (dative plural adjective agreement).

lines.original: Das kommt mir nicht aus dem Sinn.
lines.english: It will not depart from my mind.
lines.gloss: Das = 'which' (demonstrative/relative, neuter); kommt = 'comes' (kommen); mir = 'to me' (dative); aus dem Sinn = 'out of the mind' (prep + dative).

lines.original: Die Luft ist kühl und es dunkelt,
lines.english: The air is cool and it darkens,
lines.gloss: Die Luft = 'the air' (nominative feminine); ist = 'is'; kühl = 'cool'; und = 'and'; es dunkelt = 'it grows dark' (impersonal use of dunkeln).
Und = 'and'; ruhig = 'calmly'; fließt = 'flows' (fließen); der Rhein = 'the Rhine' (nominative).
Der Gipfel = 'the peak' (nominative); des Berges = 'of the mountain' (genitive); funkelt = 'sparkles, glitters' (funkeln).
Im = 'in the' (contraction of in dem, dative); Abendsonnenschein = 'evening-sun-shine' (compound noun, masculine dative).
